newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 18.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 18.

text.p: ------------------------- WAM ------------------------ ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST..... ------------------- July 18, 1997------------------ Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends *********************************************** ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

HOUSTON - Consumer products giant Procter & Gamble Co. files a federal lawsuit seeking to block Amway Corp. and its millions of distributors from associating P&G and its products with Satan. But Amway says it has denounced the "rumour" that P&G's "Moon and Stars" trademark is a satanic symbol appearing on P&G products with the number 666, the biblical mark of the devil. *********
HAMBURG - German advertising agency Baader, Lang, Behnken plans a management and ownership reshuffle, its owner, advertising group AP Lintas, says. *********

LOS ANGELES - California launches an aggressive anti-tobacco advertising campaign aimed at the state's large ethnic minority population. The campaign features a series of billboard ads, TV commercials and radio spots in Spanish and four Asian languages, as well as English, and highlights the dangers of secondhand smoke and the tobacco industry's alleged targeting of children in its advertising. *********
DALLAS - The Southland Corp., operator of 7-Eleven convenience stores, has launched new national TV and radio ad campaign created by The Richards Group of Dallas. *********

CHICAGO - Kraft Pizza Co launches its DiGiorno Rising Crust Pizza in the U.S. Northeast. The product expansion will be supported in the Northeast with an aggressive advertising campaign. The new product is aimed at capturing a larger share of the $26 billion U.S. pizza market. *********************************************** MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

NEW YORK - Thomson Consumer Electronics introduces the RCA Network Computer, a set-top box device that turns a television into a low-cost Internet access device and is one of the first major competitors to WebTV Networks Inc. *********

LONDON - Britain's Granada Group Plc says it has taken majority control of neighbour Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television. Granada says it has acceptances representing 53.2 percent of Yorkshire's share capital for a deal worth some 680 million pounds ($1.1 billion). *********

BERLIN - Publishing house Axel Springer Verlag AG posts first half net profits of over 100 million marks ($55.8 million), compared to 80.5 million in the same period a year earlier. Group operating profit reaches 229 million marks, up from 156 million marks. *********
ARLINGTON, Virginia - Gannett Co Inc says it is forming a group to handle sale of national and regional advertising for its daily newspapers, excluding USA Today. *********
LONDON - Scottish Media Group Plc says it has received acceptances for around 55.4 pct of the issued share capital in Grampian Television Plc. *********

JOHANNESBURG - South African news and information vendor INET says it has entered a joint venture deal with global information group Bridge Information Systems. *********************************************** BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

MIAMI - James Morgan, chief executive of Philip Morris Cos, the world's biggest cigarette maker, testifies in a landmark $5 billion smoking case that smoking could be "psychologically habit-forming" but is far from physically addictive. *********

LONDON - The small-car sector is set to show a boom in production over the next five years, with worldwide output seen surging by 36 percent between 1996 and 2002, according to the latest Economist Intelligence Unit survey. *********

CHICAGO - McDonald's Corp, which says it is still on track for record earnings in 1997, says U.S. operating income this year will not reach its target of a mid-single-digit percentage growth rate. *********

PARIS - French luxury goods group LVMH will have to pay British merger partners Guinness and Grand Metropolitan Plc a premium if it wants a drinks merger in which it would be the leading shareholder with 35 percent, analysts say. *********

JOHANNESBURG - South African drinks and sweets firm Cadbury Schweppes SA Ltd is set to post healthy half year growth next week, buoyed by good local demand. South Africans' taste for the firm's range of soft drinks and chocolate bars has not diminished despite a slow down in the broader economy. *********
TOKYO - Nissan Motor Co Ltd says its vehicle exports in June rose 31.3 percent from a year earlier to 62,857 units. *********

REDMOND, Washington - Microsoft Corp. reports an 88 percent rise in fiscal fourth quarter profit, reflecting strong sales of its Windows NT software and Office suite applications. *********************************************** CONSUMER TRENDS:
JOHANNESBURG - A group of Cape Town companies says that they have pledged 5.5 million rand ($1.2 million) to the South African city's bid to host the 2004 Olympic Games. *********
BONN - As Germans head south in droves for summer holidays, motorway service stations have hired teams of sport and nutrition experts to help drivers beat the stress of hours on the road. *********

WASHINGTON - The Senate agrees to pull the plug on computer games in government offices and bar the government from buying any new computers with games already loaded. "The taxpayers don't need to be paying the salaries of people who are playing games while on official time," says Sen. Lauch Faircloth. *********

SHANGHAI - Around 10 percent of households in Beijing, Guangzhou and Shanghai now have computers, up from six percent in 1996, the Wen Hui Bao newspaper says. *********************************************** -- London Advertising Newsdesk +44 171 542 2792 *********************************************** See full stories on Reuters Advertising & Media Briefing.
